+# Resolve observations; select a role only when reporting
+
+## Usage, caller's view
+
+Proposal for discussion before implementation: keep donor, payer and ultimate-payer reporting as explicit, separate views. Do not publish a single selected funder. A donor view answers who was declared as donor; an ultimate-payer view answers who was explicitly named as ultimate payer. A missing ultimate payer stays unknown even when the donor has a company number.
+
+The proposed `declarations resolve --key <ingestion-key>` stage reads the existing cleaned pair and publishes an observation-to-company mapping offline. It neither fetches registry records nor rewrites funding amounts. Exact command spelling follows the existing CLI when implemented.
+
+```rust
+// CLI: the filesystem adapter already owns the explicit ingestion key.
+let summary = DeclarationResolverService::new(storage)
+    .resolve_declarations().await?;
+println!("{} observations linked", summary.company_links());
+
+// Consumer: explicitly ask the donor question, one row per occurrence.
+let resolved = ResolvedDeclarations::new(cleaned, mapping)?;
+for occurrence in resolved.funding_view(FunderRole::Donor) {
+    display(occurrence.entry(), occurrence.observation(), occurrence.resolution());
+}
+
+// Consumer: ultimate-payer coverage includes absent and withheld observations.
+let ultimate_rows = resolved.funding_view(FunderRole::UltimatePayer);
+let coverage = count_available_names(ultimate_rows); // Not an identity count.
+```
+
+## Problem
+
+The current `funder_id` names a source-role observation. Equal names do not establish identity, and donor company evidence does not belong to an ultimate payer. The legacy preferred-name rule mixes those questions. The next useful step is narrower: join observations carrying compatible source-reported company identifiers while leaving attribution visible to callers. This uses the cleaner's role references and stable occurrence IDs without changing the database's current unique-name model.
+
+## Shape and module ownership
+
+| Module | Owns |
+| --- | --- |
+| `domain/models/declaration_resolution.rs` | Company-number parsing policy, observation outcomes, deterministic mapping, checked aggregate and explicit role views. Private collection fields prevent bypassing link invariants. |
+| `domain/repositories/declaration_resolution.rs` | Read a coherent typed cleaned dataset; publish a complete resolution artifact. No Arrow types escape. |
+| `domain/services/declaration_resolution.rs` | One read/resolve/publish operation and summary; matches `DeclarationCleanerService`. |
+| `outbound/declaration_resolution.rs` | Cleaned Parquet decoding, manifest digests, mapping encoding and atomic publication. Reuse filesystem paths and existing error conventions. |
+| `inbound/cli.rs` and ingestion-stage enum | Add offline `resolve`; require key and loader configuration only. |
+
+The service hides integrity checks, deterministic grouping and publication behind one call. The consumer supplies only the role its report means. Roles remain the existing `FunderRole` enum; there is no second list of role names. The pure model owns resolution, while the adapter parses wire fields and rejects structural corruption, per `boundary-discipline`.
+
+```rust
+// Signature sketch; bodies intentionally omitted. Existing ID and role types are reused.
+pub struct ReportedCompanyNumber(String); // Private canonical eight-character token.
+pub enum CompanyNumberEvidence {
+    Absent,
+    Accepted(ReportedCompanyNumber),
+    UnsupportedFormat { raw: String },
+}
+impl CompanyNumberEvidence {
+    pub fn parse(raw: Option<&str>) -> Self;
+}
+pub struct CompanyIdentityKey(ReportedCompanyNumber);
+pub enum UnresolvedReason {
+    NoCompanyNumber,
+    UnsupportedCompanyNumber,
+    ConflictingDonorKind,
+    UnsupportedDonorKind,
+}
+pub enum ObservationResolution {
+    SourceReportedCompany { key: CompanyIdentityKey },
+    Unresolved { reason: UnresolvedReason },
+}
+pub struct ObservationMapping {
+    observation: FunderObservationId,
+    resolution: ObservationResolution,
+}
+pub struct ResolutionMapping { rows: Vec<ObservationMapping> }
+impl ResolutionMapping {
+    pub fn resolve(cleaned: &CleanedDeclarations) -> Self;
+}
+pub struct ResolvedDeclarations {
+    cleaned: CleanedDeclarations,
+    mapping: ResolutionMapping,
+    // Private observation-ID index; validated once, then reused by role views.
+}
+pub struct FundingRoleView<'a> {
+    // Private references to exactly one entry, zero/one observation and its outcome.
+    entry: &'a CleanedFundingEntry,
+    observation: Option<&'a FunderObservation>,
+    resolution: Option<&'a ObservationResolution>,
+}
+impl ResolvedDeclarations {
+    pub fn new(cleaned: CleanedDeclarations, mapping: ResolutionMapping)
+        -> Result<Self, EntityIngestionError>;
+    pub fn funding_view(&self, role: FunderRole)
+        -> impl Iterator<Item = FundingRoleView<'_>>;
+}
+// FundingRoleView has read-only entry(), observation(), resolution() accessors.
+pub trait DeclarationResolutionStorage: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static {
+    fn read_cleaned_declarations(&self)
+        -> impl Future<Output = Result<CleanedDeclarations, EntitySearchPipelineError>> + Send;
+    fn publish_resolution(&self, result: &ResolutionMapping)
+        -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), EntitySearchPipelineError>> + Send;
+}
+pub struct DeclarationResolverService<S> { storage: S }
+impl<S: DeclarationResolutionStorage> DeclarationResolverService<S> {
+    pub const fn new(storage: S) -> Self;
+    pub async fn resolve_declarations(&self)
+        -> Result<DeclarationResolutionSummary, EntityIngestionError>;
+}
+```
+
+## Behavior contract and attribution policy
+
+| Evidence | Proposed interpretation |
+| --- | --- |
+| Donor and ultimate payer both named | Preserve both. Each role view selects only its own observation, even if names match. |
+| Ultimate payer explicitly empty or withheld | Ultimate-payer view reports missing or withheld; never falls back to donor. |
+| Ultimate-payer flag `true` | Preserve the claim of difference; absent ultimate-payer name remains unknown. No parent fallback. |
+| Flag `false` | Preserve the flag; do not equate role identities or transfer identifiers. |
+| Flag absent | Unknown flag, distinct from `false`; no implied agreement. |
+| Donor and payer names disagree | Both remain usable role observations. Neither overrides the other. |
+| Top-level names and nested occurrences | Declaration observations resolve independently; never propagate them to nested funding entries. |
+| Parent reference | Keep source reference; no inherited payer, amount, name or company number. |
+
+`FieldGroup::parent_payer_applies` returns `field.value is not True`; its caller suppresses parent fallback when the flag is true. This documents an attribution guard, not proof that false means the donor and ultimate payer are the same entity. The field's exact role semantics remain unresolved. Different names with false, or identical names with true, remain visible source tensions rather than dataset errors or identity rules.
+
+Declaration-only observations do not carry every declaration-level flag or parent reference in the cleaned tables. This design makes no declaration-level flag inference and does not pretend those omitted values are absent in the source. Source replay would be required before implementing broader declaration attribution.
+
+Company parsing trims outer whitespace and uppercases ASCII letters; it preserves every digit, including leading zeros. Version 1 accepts exactly eight ASCII alphanumeric characters containing at least one digit as a conservative token envelope. This is an explicit supported-format policy, not a catalogue of valid Companies House prefixes or proof of registry membership. Other nonblank forms produce `UnsupportedCompanyNumber`; never pad, delete punctuation, infer a country, or call an API. Empty input is absent. Retain the original value through the observation reference.
+
+The identity namespace is `source-reported:companies-house:<canonical-token>`. Its claim means that Parliament supplied this company identifier, not that the registry independently confirmed it. Missing donor kind or explicit `Company` permits that link. Explicit incompatible kinds produce `ConflictingDonorKind`; unknown kind text produces `UnsupportedDonorKind`. A conflicted observation stays unresolved even if another observation with the same number resolves. No last-write-wins entity kind exists.
+
+Two eligible observations with the same identifier share a key despite different names. Different identifiers always remain different keys. Names, aliases, initials and token similarity do not merge any identities. Withheld names and missing names can still resolve from eligible identifier evidence. Personal-looking names or conjunctions are not split or classified from spelling; a compatible captured number still makes only a source-reported company claim. Otherwise each observation remains unresolved, with its original name status available to reports.
+
+Current payer and ultimate-payer observations cannot receive a company link because cleaning attaches company numbers only to donors. Even an exact donor-name match does not change that. This limited coverage is honest and can expand later through a separately justified identity-evidence rule.
+
+## Offline artifacts, consistency and counting
+
+Publish `resolved/declarations/observation_resolution.parquet` plus a manifest. The table has exactly one row per observation: `observation_id`, `outcome`, nullable `company_identity_key`, nullable `unresolved_reason`. Outcome-specific column constraints come from the domain enum. The manifest records schema/resolver versions, input-file SHA-256 digests and row counts. No separate entity table or preferred-name record is necessary. For display, use the linked observation's original name, or the reported number if unnamed.
+
+Sort mapping rows by observation ID. Identity keys are independent of ingestion key and row order; unresolved observations get no invented shared entity key. Observation IDs remain scoped to the manifest's exact dataset, since ordinal changes between captures can change their meaning. Equal keys across runs express equal source-reported identifiers, not a claim that observations are unchanged.
+
+The adapter reads each cleaned file once into the checked dataset and binds its publication to those input digests. Reject missing columns, invalid enums, duplicate observation/occurrence IDs, wrong role/scope references, inconsistent ordinals and dangling funding references before writing. Malformed company strings, withheld names and conflicting donor kinds are row outcomes and do not fail the run. Missing files and read/write failures use storage errors; structural input failures use the existing data/read-error conventions with path context.
+
+Write both artifacts into a unique sibling staging directory, close and sync them, then publish with an atomic no-replace directory operation. A completed existing destination is an explicit error; a repeat never silently overwrites. Concurrent attempts own different staging directories and only one can publish, per `separate-before-serializing-shared-state`. A crash leaves either a complete result or an ignored staging directory. A future policy version requires a new run/output location, not editing an existing artifact.
+
+Each role view iterates funding entries first and follows at most one role reference. It emits one row for every occurrence, including absent roles, so an amount appears once per view. A report must choose one view for financial totals; unioning roles is a relationship report, not an additive money table. To ask whether a company occurs in any role, select distinct funding-entry IDs before joining amounts. Declaration-scoped observations never create funding rows. Currency/amount parsing remains outside this identity stage.
+
+## Acceptance cases
+
+| Input | Required result |
+| --- | --- |
+| `Acme Ltd / 01234567` and `Acme Holdings / 01234567` on eligible donors | One company key, two observations; all occurrences retained. |
+| Same donor name with `01234567` and `07654321` | Two company keys; no name bridge. |
+| Donor has number; identical ultimate-payer name | Donor resolves; ultimate payer remains unresolved. |
+| Donor named; ultimate payer withheld; flag true | Ultimate view keeps withheld observation, with no fallback. |
+| Flag false with different role names; flag absent in another entry | Both retain separate observations; no asserted same-entity relation. |
+| `1234567`, `SC-12345`, whitespace-only identifier | Unsupported, unsupported, absent respectively; no fabricated digits. |
+| ` sc123456 ` and `SC123456`, eligible kinds | Same source-reported key; no registry-verification claim. |
+| Number with `Individual`; same number elsewhere with `Company` | Individual observation unresolved; compatible company observation resolves. |
+| Missing/withheld name with eligible number | Company link with name status unchanged. |
+| `Jane Doe`, `A and B`, no number | Separate unresolved observations; no person merge or splitting. |
+| Top-level payer, two nested entries lacking payer, parent reference | Declaration observation retained; two missing payer-view rows, no inheritance. |
+| Duplicate identical payments | Distinct occurrence IDs and two view rows; no deduplication by name/value. |
+| Malformed reference, I/O failure, existing final destination | Fail with no new completed output. |
+
+## Tradeoffs, alternatives and review
+
+We accept unresolved payer identities and explicit report-role selection in exchange for a small, auditable identity rule. We accept conservative unsupported-number outcomes rather than guessing corrections. The most consequential product decision remains this proposal to offer separate role views without a preferred funder.
+
+A typed payment-attribution decision model would hide fallback and withholding rules behind a single answer per occurrence. It is better once the user chooses a preferred funding question, but today it would encode unsettled role semantics into every result. A general relationship graph would express inherited payer and controller relationships, but callers would need traversal and cardinality rules for ordinary totals. The mapping plus fixed role views hides those joins without introducing that graph language.
+
+Red-flag screening: no public Arrow schemas; no duplicated role registry; one pure owner of company eligibility and identity keys; one publication writer; no intermediate persistence stages; no generic matching engine or pass-through search service. The service's storage boundary is justified by offline I/O and atomic publication, not merely forwarding a model call. A consumer cannot construct an unchecked aggregate or modify its private indexes.
+
+Synthesis decision: reserved for the parent architect. Implementation reconciliation: none; this package contains no implementation.
+
+Open question for the checkpoint: does the user want these explicit role views, or a single preferred-funder report with a separately approved fallback policy? Is the deliberately conservative eight-character token envelope sufficient for the captured data, with unsupported values reported for later review?
+
+After the user has been taught and accepted the design, first implement the checked cleaned-input reader and pure mapping against the acceptance cases. No database schema change or website search dependency is needed; any later database adapter must use SQLx macros.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
Completed candidate 1 in `.design/funder-resolution/candidate-1/design.md`.

The design separates company identity mapping from derived reporting views, supports explicit same-member parent-payer attribution for flag false, preserves provenance, and avoids name-based metadata transfer. It includes Rust signatures, policy and acceptance tables, publication rules, alternatives, and red-flag screening.

No application changes or implementation.
